paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua. (a) Mishnah Avot, chapter 4; Gittin 3:8; Temurah 3:3, 4:4 [the latter mishnah names Elazar son of Shimon]; Chagigah 12b. He is unqualified Rabbi Elazar in Mishnah and baraita: Rashi, Shabbat 19, beginning of b; Eruvin 38b; Yevamot 72b, 111b; Gittin 31b; Ketubbot 40a. Tosafot, Bava Batra 156: read Elazar, not Eliezer ben Hyrcanus; see there. Avot, chapter 2, has unqualified R.A. meaning Elazar ben Arakh: context explains it.

(b) Sifrei, Re'eh, “When the Lord your God cuts off”: he went with Yochanan Hassandlar to study with Yehudah ben Beteira and Yehudah ben Shammua; see there. [The checked Sifrei names Yehudah ben Beteira alone.] Rashi, Ketubbot 40a: Akiva’s student, as Haba Al Yevimto. After Akiva’s students died, the world was desolate until he taught the southern masters: Meir, Yehudah, Yose, Shimon, Elazar ben Shammua. Zevachim, chapter 11, 93, 110b, and Ketubbot there: Elazar follows his teacher Akiva’s position. Yehudah ben Bava ordained him. He taught Rabbi: Yevamot 84a, Rabbi says, “When I went to study with Elazar ben Shammua, his students surrounded me like Beit Bukya’s cocks, allowing me to learn only one matter of our Mishnah.” Yoma 79b: “When we studied with Elazar ben Shammua.” Hakometz 18a: “When I went to exhaust my measures”—some say Shammua’s measures—“I found Yosef the Babylonian before him”; see Issi ben Akiva. Eruvin 53a: “We sat six in one cubit.” Yochanan: earlier scholars’ hearts were like the porch entrance, later ones the sanctuary entrance: earlier Akiva, later Shammua; alternatively, earlier Shammua, later Oshaya (see Akiva). Menachot 22a puts Elazar son of Shimon, Rabbi’s colleague, before Shammua, Rabbi’s teacher; see my rules.

(c) Yevamot, chapter 6; Sotah 39; Benei Ha'ir 27: he was a priest. He blessed before raising hands, never used a synagogue as a shortcut or stepped over the holy people’s heads; therefore lived long, Bamidbar Rabbah 11. Rav called him tuvayna de-chakhimei, Gittin 26b; Ketubbot 40a; Keritot 13b. Rashi: most fortunate of sages; Rav Tzemach: exceptional in wisdom. Last of the ten royal martyrs, killed Friday night at kiddush’s “which God created to do.” A heavenly voice: “Happy are you, Elazar My son! In this world your soul resembled God, and departed with ‘God.’” I wonder: he taught Rabbi, whose time apparently had no persecution. Though Rashi, end of Ein Makkirin, explains “Go to Ein Tav and sanctify the month” as persecution, his alternative explanation seems right. At his death a Torah scroll was hidden away, Mishnah, Eglah Arufah [the similar report in the Bavli baraita reads Eliezer].

(d) Abba Eliezer ben Dola'ai in his time. “Eliezer said in Eliezer’s name,” [the checked Tosefta Terumot gives Elazar as reporter, followed by an abbreviation] Tosefta, end of Terumot, chapter 3, and end of Menachot. Elazar says: Eliezer invalidates, Yehoshua permits. “We told Meir”: Rashi, Gittin 12b, says a colleague, hence not called Rabbi. Elazar: “At Ardaski I found Meir and Yehudah ben Beteira. ‘Meir, did you know Yehoshua ben Mammal?’ ‘Yes; versed in law.’” Tosefta, Nazir, chapter 5. Nazir 56b, Mishnah and Gemara, “Eliezer said in Yehoshua’s name,” and “At Ardaskya I found Meir,” are errors for Elazar, namely Shammua, Etz Chayyim’s commentary there. Yose ben Yehudah in his name—requires examination; Yose ben Kippur in his name; Yose ben Perida, his student. In Yose the Galilean’s name; Yehudah ben Beteira’s name.
